title: I made a farm/idle game with my daughter — AMA about dev/features!
author: mendlogames
selftext:
Hey r/aigamedev,

This year I've been building **Miners, Moos & Miracles**, an idle/incremental farm-and-adventure game (Godot 4 + C#) where you run a little homestead and dip into a bunch of themed mini-games — a demon-fighting mine, cow soccer, cooking recipes, chicken coop egg-collection, fish tank care and character customization — all wrapped in a retro CRT-styled shell.

The best part of this project has been making it with my daughter. She tested builds, gave me feedback on what was fun (and what wasn't), and made all of the music in the game. Getting to build something together like this has been one of the most rewarding parts of the whole process.

On the AI side: I used generative AI (Claude) to help make the procedural visuals and sound effects in the game. No third-party art assets. Everything's drawn in code. Happy to talk about that workflow too since that's what this sub is about.  
  
🛒 Coming to Steam this month: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4995840/Miners\_Moos\_\_Miracles/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4995840/Miners_Moos__Miracles/)

**Ask me anything** — engine choices, the mini-game design, using AI in the art/dev pipeline, what it's like making a game with a kid, whatever you're curious about. Happy to answer!
